When SpaceX isn't busy recovering rockets, it turns out they've been busy acquiring AI companies. In February this year, the company behind Starlink brought xAI under its umbrella, which also includes the X platform formerly known as Twitter. In April, SpaceX signed a deal with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. SpaceXAI—now known by this name—recently launched the Grok Bot and Grok 4.6 model with Cursor's assistance.

Update (August 14, 2026): SpaceXAI has completed the acquisition of Cursor.

Update (June 16, 2026): SpaceX acquired Cursor a week after going public.

The original article has been updated as follows:

SpaceX strikes $10 billion deal with Cursor ahead of $60 billion acquisition

Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who use AI to code on Mac. It was one of the earliest services to combine large language model AI with the application development workflow.

In April this year, SpaceX and Cursor said the two companies were "working closely together to build the world's leading AI for coding and knowledge work".

The original collaboration included SpaceX paying Cursor $10 billion:

In April—before this acquisition—Cursor further revealed details of the partnership:

Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. Composer was first released six months ago as our first agentic coding model. Subsequently, Composer 1.5 scaled reinforcement learning by more than 20 times. Composer 2 added continued pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a cost far lower than other models. With each level of compute scale, model capabilities grow substantially. We've always wanted to push our training work further, but have been constrained by compute. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to significantly boost our models' intelligence.

The SpaceX-Cursor collaboration has further strengthened a competitor capable of taking on Claude Code from Anthropic and OpenAI's Codex agentic coding software.
